text: Network-dependent apps are rejected under 2.1 when the reviewer cannot reach the back end or sign in (geo-blocked API, expired demo credentials, OTP the reviewer cannot receive, IPv6-only test network). This is reported by secondary blogs and forums, not stated by Apple as a statistic. (low confidence)

text: Guideline 2.1 requires final builds, working URLs, demo account info and a live back-end service for any login; if a demo account is impossible for legal or security reasons, a built-in demo mode needs prior Apple approval and must show full functionality. Crashing or obviously broken binaries are rejected. (high confidence)

text: Rejected or Metadata Rejected submissions are answered in Resolution Center; Apple says replies generally arrive within 24 hours and screenshots can be attached. Login instructions, feature locations and demo accounts belong in the App Review Information / Notes for Review fields. (high confidence)

text: If still disputed after a Resolution Center reply, the developer files an appeal to the App Review Board via a link in App Store Connect / the Contact Us form; the appeal must be specific about how the app complies. Secondary sources report one appeal per developer account and a 14-day window, and no published turnaround (often a week or more). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-02)

text: Guideline 2.3 forbids hidden, dormant or undocumented features and requires new features to be described in Notes for Review; an optional AI/alert integration should be explicitly described there, with how to enable it. (medium confidence)

text: Mac App Store utilities hit Guideline 2.4.5: must be sandboxed, no root escalation or setuid, no login auto-launch without consent, no downloading code or resources that change functionality, updates only via Mac App Store. Apple denies temporary-exception entitlements such as com.apple.security.temporary-exception.sbpl allow iokit-open (CPU temperature readers) under 2.4.5(i). (medium confidence)
